previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC syndrome, and prior port infections was admitted for headaches, nausea, vomiting, and a supratherapeutic INR of 7.3. Initial concerns included intracranial bleed or infection, but brain MRI showed no acute findings. Her symptoms were attributed to a combination of factors: bacterial overgrowth from recent antibiotics, managed with metronidazole; aspiration pneumonia, diagnosed on chest X-ray and treated with levofloxacin; and a yeast vaginitis, treated with topical antifungals. Her INR normalized after holding warfarin, and she was restarted on her home dose. The pelvic MRI showed improvement in her prior pectineus abscess with no fluid collection. She responded well to treatment, with resolution of headaches, nausea, and fevers, and was discharged home on a 7-day course of oral antibiotics and antifungal therapy, with instructions to continue her home medications and follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
In summary, the patient is a ___ female with longstanding 
history of Crohn's Disease with frequent flare-ups, short bowel 
syndrome, numerous line infections,  history of SVC syndrome (on 
anticoagulation) who presented on this admission with complaints 
of headache, nausea, and vomiting. Noted major conditions during 
this hospitalization included Bacillus Cereus/Thuringiensis 
bacteremia, Crohn's flare-up and migraines. Details outlined 
below: 
.
#. Headaches: Initial headaches concerning for neurological 
disease such as stroke or increased intracranial pressure 
because patient reported transient neurological findings 
including right facial droop, right arm weakness, slurred 
speech. However, these issues all resolved by the time she 
reached OSH ED and there were no focal neurological deficits on 
her exam here in the ED or after admisssion to the medical floor 
on serial neurological testing. A noncontrast head CT at ___ as 
reviewed with ___ radiologist and was negative for any bleeds 
or IC pathology. Of relevance, last hospital admission a few 
weeks prior included a negative Head MRI/MRA and unremarkable 
neurological consult for similar chief complaint. Given negative 
imaging, mild photophobia, nausea and vomiting, migraine 
headaches were entertained as the primary etiology. Her sister 
also has classic migraines as well. Discerning her nausea and 
vomiting from her usual Crohn's Disease flare ups was 
challenging however. Especially, since she felt she had been 
having ""off and on"" Crohn's symptoms for a month. It was felt 
that her description of blue lights in her vision was an aura, 
as it was closely followed by a bifrontal/then right sided 
headache that ""throbbed"".  She was placed on sumatriptan which 
had good effect. Given her frequent bacteremias and extensive 
PMH of line infections, however, meningitis was also high on the 
differential list and on hospital day 2 she spiked fevers to the 
101-102 range so an LP was done, but returned negative. She was 
later found to have bacteremia which was perhaps a trigger for 
her migraine presentation.  
.
#Nausea/Vomiting/Diarrhea: Although her Sumatriptan helped her 
headaches she continued to have intermittent nausea, diarrhea, 
bloating and vomiting. These symptoms tapered by time of 
discharge and were ultimately felt to be more a feature of her 
ongoing Crohn's Disease and short-gut malabsorption issues as 
opposed to a feature specific to her migraines. In regards to 
her diarrhea, a follow-up C.difficile stool was negative and 
occasional diarrhea is a chronic issue which is due to her 
known, extensive GI surgeries/Crohn's. Patient had a benign 
abdomen on admission but complained of RLQ abdominal pain 
intermittently throughout her hospitalization, as well as dry 
heaves/nausea. No guarding or rebound on exam. CT abdomen/pelvis 
WNL.  GI team consulted and felt she had ongoing ileus issues 
with improving distension.  Mrs. ___ felt her symptoms were 
typical of her ""Crohn's flare ups"". As she is allergic to Zofran 
and Reglan, anti-nausea therapy was challenging. She claimed 
Benadryl and Dilaudid were the only medications that offered her 
relief, these were given with plan of PO taper on discharge. 
However, at time of discharge the patient expressed that she 
wanted additional Dilauded which was refused as she had been 
given a full script per OMR records just 6 days prior to her 
admission. This was discussed with her PCP prior to discharge 
who agreed with the written PO taper planned. Patient was set up 
for a close follow-up outpatient appointment with PCP the day 
after discharge to discuss her concerns and narcotics agreement 
at greater length.    
.
#Bacteremia / Fevers: After fevers in 101-102 range on hospital 
day ___, LP was performed and was negative.Due to concerning 
high fevers the ID team consulted and recommended CT 
Abdomen/Pelvis for review of possible gut sources given Crohn's 
history and pectineus muscle abscess a few months prior. CT 
abd/pelvis showed no evidence for abdominal fluid collection, 
fistula, inflammatory stranding, or bowel wall thickening. Some 
ground-glass opacities still visualized at ___ consistent with 
her known resolving PNA. Port-a-cath site had no local 
edema/erythema, discharge or tenderness. However, it has been in 
place for several months and was felt to be the source of her 
bacteremia. Several blood cultures were collected off of her 
right sided port-a-catheter line and returned positive for gram 
positive rods. Subsequent microbiology testing confirmed 
Bacillus Cereus/Th___ species. Thus, her headaches and 
nausea may have been partly related to bacteremia. She was 
continued on Tylenol PRN for fevers and headaches as well as 
Sumatriptan PRN up to 200mg per day for migraine relief. 
Follow-up TTE showed no vegatations. Bacillus R/S came back and 
were sensitive to Levofloxacin/Gentamycin/Clindamycin so she was 
continued on Levofloxacin PO regimen. Prior to this final 
positive blood culture report, she had been placed on Vancomycin 
and Zosyn for a few days and then she was eventually switched to 
PO levaquin. After much discussion with the surgical service her 
PAC was removed on ___ with no noted complications. She had 
no leukocytosis despite positive cultures and initial fevers.  
MR ___ done on ___ mainly for reassurance that there 
were future access options given her history of very difficult 
central access. Venograms  showed patent internal jugular veins, 
brachiocephalic veins and superior vena cava, occluded 
subclavian veins bilaterally and occluded external iliac veins 
bilaterally, & patent IVC and bilateral common iliac veins with 
lower extremity venous return primarily through the internal 
iliac veins. On ___ patient spiked fever to 101 degrees 
after port-a-cath removed. This was felt to be a post-operative 
spike in the setting of possible re-entry into systemic flow 
from removal process and team monitored her closely for 
improvement for ___ more days before considering 
discharge.Additional urine cultures and follow up repeat blood 
cultures were negative with the exception of a right 
port-a-catheter chamber swab collected around the time of her 
port-a-cath removal and confirmed as positive for Bacillus 
species/rare growth and some additional rare growth of coagulase 
negative staphylococcus was also identified.
She was afebrile at discharge and she was continued on PO 
Levaquin after discharge for just under 3 weeks of total 
therapy, and she was set-up for an ___ follow-up 
appointment in early ___. 
.
# Right Pneumonia: repeat venogram noted areas of right lung 
patchy infiltrate and repeat CXR on ___ showed resolving 
RUL/RML/RLL multifocal PNA which was known from prior admission. 
Clinically, the patient's lung sounds were mildly decreased on 
the right side but improved during her hospital course, she had 
no leukocytosis, no cough, no chills, and had been afebrile for 
several days prior to discharge. ID team consulted and felt she 
was appropriately covered on her Levaquin regimen. CXR note of 
PNA expected given that radiologically PNA evidence often lags 
for several weeks after effective treatment is complete. She 
will plan to follow-up additional imaging as needed in the 
future at her PCP and ID ___ should her clinical PNA 
symptoms return.  
.
#Left Knee Pain: Overnight on ___ into ___ the patient 
got up to go to the bath room and got ""caught up"" in her sheets 
and had a brief fall and struck her left knee on the floor. She 
denied any other impacts, and claimed she had no LOC and stated 
she did not hit her head or any other extremity other than her 
left knee. On inspection there is some mild edema at lower, 
medial joint aspect but no clear bruising, warmth. She had 
tenderness to palpation of medial joint line near tibial 
prominence and some minimal joint pain with extension and valgus 
stress testing. Negative McMurray testing. X-rays obtained and 
plain left knee films showed suprapatellar swelling/small 
effusion and mild osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral and 
medial compartments of the left knee joint but no dislocations, 
or fractures identified. She was given her written 
Dilaudid/Tylenol for pain control, and her knee was elevated 
with ice pack application. She was advised to follow-up with her 
PCP as needed as an outpatient if her pain did not subside 
completely in a few weeks. She was also placed on fall 
precautions. 
.
#.Right arm swelling -On admission the patient complained of 
some right wrist and forearm swelling. She had a right upper 
extremity doppler which was unremarkable and negative for any 
DVTs.  She continued to describe a band-like tightness and 
""bumps and lesions"" on right forearm that had spontaneously 
resolved prior to evaluation and were not noted again during her 
hospital course. No edema noted on exam despite her subjective 
sense of feeling swollen. This gradually resolved,  asymptomatic 
and no complaints at time of discharge. 
.
#. Hypokalemia / Hypomagnesemia: Chronic ongoing electrolyte 
depletions from malabsorption issues. These electrolyte changes 
were monitored daily and IV and PO repletion were given as 
needed. 
.
#High lactate. Initial lactate was elevated to 7 range.   This 
was likely multifactorial; infection going on with gram positive 
rod blood cultures and patient got 2L lactated ringers IVFs 
overnight on ___. Soon afterwards, additional labs were 
trended and lactate normalized over 24 hours to 2.6 and then to 
1.8.
.
#. Anemia: Patient with known history of iron deficiency anemia, 
likely secondary to poor absorption and short gut syndrome. Hct 
on admission was higher than baseline. Hct trended during her 
hospital course and fell to a nadir of 21 on ___. She was 
given 1 Unit of blood on ___ and Hct went up to 26.3. 
Hematocrit then remained stable in ___ range up until time of 
discharge. She was set up for an outpatient follow-up with 
Heme/Oncology after discharge to further investigate her anemia 
and frequent fleeting leukopenias noticed over her last few 
hospitalizations. 
.
#. Hypothyroidism: Chronic condition, stable. She was continued 
on her usual home levothyroxine therapy. 
.
#. Depression/anxiety: Mrs. ___ was emotionally labile on 
admission and noncompliant with medication requests. She 
mentioned that she had stopped her prior celexa medication over 
a month prior due to bad dreams. During this admission a 
psychiatry consult was called and social work also visited Mrs. 
___ for coping support.  She was continued on Valium PRN for 
anxiety episodes and psychiatry recommended additional Haldol at 
low doses PRN. She was given contact information for outpatient 
psychiatric follow-up at time of discharge for her PTSD/Anxiety 
and Depression symptoms. Whenever possible interaction with male 
staff, especially alone in 1:1 encounters, were avoided given 
her history of PTSD and prior rape incidents. 
.
#Fibromyalgia: She was continued on her home Dilaudid/Tylenol. 
.
#Leukopenia: The patient had transient drops in her WBC counts 
into the ___ range. This was thought to be a medication reaction 
to Zosyn/Vanco as her WBC counts have risen since she has 
discontinued these medications and switched to Levaquin. WBC 
levels are still below normal range, however, and she was set up 
for Heme/Onc follow-up at discharge to explore this issue 
further. Immunoglobulin levels were checked for question of CVID 
or other more isolated deficiencies but IgA, IgM levels WNL.   
.

#.SVC syndrome - Mrs. ___ gets ongoing anticoagulation with 
Warfarin for her history of SVC syndrome and multiple blood 
clots. INR 2.1 at OSH prior to admission and her INR goal is 
2.5-3.5 . All Heparin products were avoided due to her history 
of + HIT. Held warfarin briefly for her PAC line removal 
___ but restarted on ___ with no noted complications. 
___ monitored closely daily. INR at discharge was 2.8 and 
she was discharged on usual 4mg Warfarin ___ and 2mg 
every other weekday with follow-up INR checks arranged via HCA.  

.
# Fluids,Electrolytes and Nutrition: She was kept on a regular 
PO diet which she tolerated well and electrolytes were monitored 
and repleted as needed. 
,
#. Prophylaxis: 
--for DVT and PE prevention, continued on Warfarin therapy
--home PPI was continued for ongoing GI protection 
.
# Communication / Code Status: The patient was maintained as a 
full code status for the entirety of her hospital course and 
communication occurred on a daily basis directly with the 
patient, and occasionally with her husband as well. PCP also 
updated regarding patient's diagnoses. 
.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with right arm swelling for one day.  Evaluate
for DVT.

RIGHT UPPER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND:  Grayscale and Doppler sonogram of
the right internal jugular, subclavian, axillary, brachial, basilic and
cephalic veins are performed.  Normal waveform, augmentation, compressibility
and flow are demonstrated.  No intraluminal thrombus is identified.

IMPRESSION:  No right upper extremity DVT.

PORTABLE CHEST ___

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Fever.

FINDINGS:

Right subclavian catheter terminates in the superior vena cava.  Compared to
the prior study, there has been interval clearing of the right upper lobe
pneumonia, although a faint patchy airspace infiltrate remains.  There is also
a vague infiltrate in the right middle lobe which has diminished in density. 
Left lung is clear.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

Interval improvement, with decreased density of right upper lobe and right
middle lobe infiltrates.

INDICATION:  Crohn's disease with right lower quadrant pain.  Fever.  Please
evaluate for fistula or abscess.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis after the uneventful intravenous
administration of 130 cc Optiray contrast displayed in 5-mm axial collimation
with multiplanar reformations.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  Ground-glass opacification in the right middle lobe
has increased from the prior study along with faint opacities in the lower
lobes.  The chest is incompletely imaged, but the findings could represent
infection.  Pancreas, spleen, stomach, adrenal glands, and kidneys are normal.
The gallbladder has been removed.  There is no free air or pathologic
adenopathy.

Patient is status post right colonic resection with neoterminal ileum in the
right upper quadrant.  The anastomosis appears normal.  The small bowel loops
are normal and nondilated.  There is no bowel wall thickening.  There is no
inflammatory stranding in the right lower quadrant.  There is no evidence for
fluid collection or fistula.  There are very small mesenteric lymph nodes.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  The rectum, sigmoid, large bowel, distal ureters,
and bladder are normal.  The uterus is not identified.

BONE WINDOWS:  There is bilateral SI joint sclerosis which is unchanged from
multiple prior studies and likely represents sacroiliitis in the setting of
Crohn's disease.

There is an area of increased soft tissue density within the subcutaneous
tissues of the anterior abdominal wall (2:58) at the site of prior midline
insertion with multiple bowel loops retracted anteriorly at this site,
unchanged from multiple prior studies and could potentially represent an area
of adhesion.  However, there is no evidence for obstruction.

Multiple calcifications are redemonstrated within the buttocks.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Worsening ground-glass opacities in the visualized portions of the lung
which could potentially represent pneumonia.
2.  No evidence for abdominal fluid collection, fistula, inflammatory
stranding, or bowel wall thickening.

MRV CHEST, ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  Crohn's disease.  Previous SVC syndrome.  Right Port-A-Cath in
place. Assess for alternative venous access site.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted imaging was acquired on a 1.5
Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior to, during, and after
the uneventful intravenous administration of 0.2 mmol/kg of gadolinium-BOPTA.
Dynamic imaging was obtained as the table translated through three stations to
cover the venous anatomy of the chest, abdomen and pelvis. Multiplanar 2D and
3D reformations were generated on an independent workstation.

COMPARISON:  MRI pelvis, ___.

FINDINGS:

MRV CHEST:

The superior vena cava is patent.  It is narrow in transverse diameter
measuring as little as 6 mm transversely.  The lateral wall of the SVC lumen
is irregular, possibly representing scarring as a result of prior central
venous catheters.  There is a Port-A-Cath in situ with its distal tip located
in the right atrium.  The internal jugular veins are patent bilaterally. These
drain into patent brachiocephalic veins bilaterally.  The brachiocephalic
veins both drain into the SVC without evidence of thrombosis or occlusion.

The subclavian veins bilaterally are essentially occluded with small
collateral veins draining the upper limbs bilaterally.

The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber without evidence of aneurysm.  The
arch vessels are normal.

There is abnormal increased signal intensity within the apical segment of the
right upper lobe.  This region enhances post-contrast.  This is compatible
with consolidation.  Linear atelectasis is also noted in the right lower lobe.

There are enlarged subcarinal and right hilar lymph nodes, measuring up to 1.6
cm in short-axis diameter.  These may be reactive.

MRV ABDOMEN:

The inferior vena cava is normal in caliber.  It is patent.

Note is made of enlarged spleen measuring 19 cm in craniocaudal dimension.  No
focal splenic lesion is identified.  No focal liver lesion is seen.  The
portal vein is patent.  There is a 7-mm simple cyst in the lower pole of the
right kidney.  There is no concerning focal renal lesion.  There is no adrenal
mass. The visualized portion of the pancreas is normal.  There is no
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  The visualized bones are normal.

MRV PELVIS:

The common iliac veins are patent bilaterally.  The internal iliac veins are
also patent.  The external iliac veins are occluded bilaterally.  The right
common femoral vein is patent to the level of the inguinal ligament at which
point it drains into small collateral vessels along the abdominal and pelvic
wall.  The left common femoral vein is patent, although irregular in caliber.
Again, at the level of the inguinal ligament, it drains via collaterals
including inferior epigastric vessels.

Residual enhancement within the pectineus muscle compatible with prior
inflammatory change as documented on previous pelvic MRIs is again seen.  No
large abscess is demonstrated, although the current study is not optimized to
evaluate this.  No abnormal osseous finding is seen in the pelvis.  There is
no pelvic fluid collection.

Multiplanar 2D and 3D reformations and subtraction images provided multiple
perspectives for the dynamic series.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Patent internal jugular veins, brachiocephalic veins and superior vena
cava.  
2.  Occluded subclavian veins bilaterally.
3.  Occluded external iliac veins bilaterally.  Patent IVC and bilateral
common iliac veins with lower extremity venous return primarily through the
internal iliac veins.
4.  Right upper lobe pneumonia.

This report was phoned to Dr. ___ at 6:30 p.m. on ___.

HISTORY:  ___ woman after fall with medial left knee tenderness and
edema.

COMPARISON:  No prior study.

LEFT KNEE, THREE VIEWS:  There is no evidence of fracture or dislocation.
There is a small suprapatellar knee effusion.  Small marginal osteophytes are
noted of the patella and of the medial knee joint compartment.  There is no
significant soft tissue swelling.

IMPRESSION:  Mild osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral and medial compartments
of the left knee joint.  Small effusion.  No fracture identified.

CHEST TWO VIEWS, ___

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Question new pneumonia, history of bacteremia, right
upper lobe pneumonia with new fever.

FINDINGS:

Compared to the prior study from ___, there is increased opacification of
the right upper lobe consistent with right upper lobe pneumonia.  The right
subclavian line has been removed.  There is also a patchy airspace opacity in
the right lower lobe and right middle lobe consistent with multilobar
pneumonia.  The left lung is relatively clear.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette
is unremarkable.

STUDY:  PA and lateral chest, ___.

HISTORY:  Patient with decreased breath sounds in the right base.  Assess for
infiltrate vs. effusion.

FINDINGS:  There is again noted patchy infiltrates within the right upper,
middle, and lower lobes.  There is margination of the greater fissure, best
seen on the lateral view.  Overall, findings are unchanged consistent with
multifocal pneumonia.  There are no pleural effusions on either side.
